_comment: Committed benchmark baseline (#1099). The Bench workflow fails when a gated benchmark runs more than `tolerance`x slower than its `mean` here, or breaches its `budgetMs` ceiling. BLESS ON CI, NEVER LOCALLY (#2211). Dispatch the Bench workflow with `update_baseline: true` at least twice and compare the artifacts; if they disagree, dispatch a third and commit the per-entry median, as #2331 did. `pnpm bench:baseline` locally is for diagnosis only. A dev machine measures ~1.2-1.4x faster than macos-latest, so a locally-blessed entry lands on CI already 'slower' and eats most of its tolerance. #2331 found that this had been true of the save-path entries all along: the indexAllNotes means were blessed locally in #1487 and the writeAndReindex / indexNote means in #1472, and CI never measured anything that low, which is part of why the gate read as a 3-3.8x regression for seven weeks. CURRENT STATE (#2331, main @ 69eb5f5f, 2026-09-28). Every entry is gated. Each mean is the per-entry MEDIAN of three `update_baseline` dispatches of the same commit, not one artifact, because the runners disagreed: one ran ~1.4-1.5x slow on both controls, and the save-path benches were bimodal by ~2x between the other two even with identical controls (they write and read real files, which the CPU-bound controls do not see). A single artifact would have put the baseline at one end of that spread and flapped on the other. The six entries #2211 added ungated (persistGraph + queryGraph, runAllChecks) are armed now that #2306 and #2330 fixed what they measure; runAllChecks FELL 2.6-4.4x despite its fixture now reaching checkStaleness, because #2330/#2309 made the sweep cheaper by more than the honest fixture added. The save-path entries are HIGHER than the old local means and are not a regression: a same-machine run of 4cf4a1bf (the #1487 blessing commit) against this commit, old fixture on both, has this commit 10-38% faster on writeAndReindex, indexNote and indexAllNotes; the new writeAndReindex fixture adds 14-29% on top. BUDGETS AND TOLERANCES. A `budgetMs` ceiling goes on only once two CI runs agree to about 1%. None was added in #2331: a few pairs agreed that closely (the tag-filter bench at 1.13ms twice), but in every case the third run landed 40%+ away, so two-run agreement was luck, not a property of the bench. The three cold-rebuild ceilings (6/12/24) set in #2211 on two agreeing runs are kept; the slowest #2331 run sits well inside them. The three indexAllNotes ceilings (220/750/1800) are REMOVED: they were 1.5x the locally-blessed means and every #2331 run breached the 500-note one. indexAllNotes 5000's 1.3x tolerance is removed for the same reason #2211 removed the queryGraph ones: its same-commit spread was 1.5x. The two queryGraph cache-hit benches carry tolerance 4 (same-commit spread 3.6x and 2.4x on a sub-millisecond bench) and cold rebuild at 5000 carries 3 (spread 2.05x; its 24ms ceiling is the tighter bound). A gate that fires on runner noise is a gate people stop reading. That is #2358. READING A FAILURE. Look at the two controls first (cosineSimilarity, meanPoolNormalize: pure CPU, no I/O). If they moved too, the runner is slow, not the code. Then compare against the previous scheduled run before bisecting. FIELDS. `budgetMs`: optional absolute ceiling in ms (a scale-envelope gate) on top of the ratio check. `tolerance`: optional per-benchmark override of the top-level ratio gate, sized to that bench's demonstrated CI noise (#1945). `gate: false`: track for week-over-week diffing but never fail on it. It REQUIRES `"issue": <number>` (the open issue that will arm it) and `"reason": "..."` (#2358): tests/architecture/bench-ungated-entries-tracked.test.ts fails without them, and bench.yml fails the run if the linked issue is closed, because a closed owner means nobody will ever arm the bench. `bench-check.mjs --update` preserves all of these and this comment across a re-bless.
